chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and Abū Baṣīr, who said: We said to him: A man frequently doubts in his salat (prayer)...

...until he does not know how much he has prayed, nor what remains upon him. He said: ‘He repeats.’ We said: But that happens to him often; whenever he repeats, he doubts. He said: ‘He should proceed despite his doubt.’ Then he said: ‘Do not habituate the wicked one from among yourselves to breaking the salat (prayer), lest you make him ambitious, for indeed Shayṭān is wicked and becomes accustomed to what he is accustomed to. So let one of you proceed in the delusion, and let him not excessively break the salat (prayer), for if he does that several times, the doubt will not return to him.’ Zurārah said: Then he said: ‘The wicked one only wants to be obeyed; so if he is disobeyed, he will not return to any one of you.’
And whoever is in his salat (prayer) and does not know what he has prayed, it is obligatory upon him to repeat the salat (prayer), and that is indicated by this.

key_terms.الشَّكُّ: doubt, the recurrent uncertainty discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْخَبِيثَ: the wicked one, referring here to Shayṭān
key_terms.الْوَهْمِ: misgiving or delusion, the baseless uncertainty one is told to disregard
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the act of ritual worship under discussion
key_terms.نَقْضَ الصَّلَاةِ: breaking the salat (prayer), i.e. invalidating or restarting it due to doubt
key_terms.يَشُكُّ: he doubts, referring to uncertainty during salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَمْضِي: he proceeds, meaning he continues without acting on the doubt
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats, meaning he performs the salat (prayer) again

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he frequently doubts during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on frequent doubt in salat (prayer), distinguishing between a state that requires repetition and recurrent misgivings that should be ignored. It teaches that one should not yield to Shayṭān’s insinuations by repeatedly breaking and restarting salat (prayer), but rather continue once such doubts become excessive.
